By training top-k sparse autoencoders on features from various different models to extract sparse attribute features, the cross-model alignment degree of these sparse features is verified to be significantly higher than that of the original dense representations, proving that the sparse linear object-attribute structure is the common Platonic signal in PRH. 2) Bias component: Model-specific factors such as architecture and training procedures introduce implicit biases to representations, leading to inconsistent alignment results under different similarity metrics. This work proposes that such biases can be partially mitigated by statistical operations such as centering and normalization. 3) Noise component: The distribution of inference data directly affects representation alignment effect; meaningful representation alignment hardly occurs on out-of-distribution data, which is consistent with existing experience in multimodal out-of-distribution detection.5e:T588,The method is a black-box search procedure for discovering spurious system prompts. A spurious prompt is defined by exclusion: it must not name or describe the target task, invoke domain-specific vocabulary, or use common reasoning cues such as asking the model to think carefully, verify answers, or eliminate options. At the same time, it must still instruct the assistant to answer the user’s query directly.

The search loop has three components: a generator produces initial candidate prompts, a validator filters them using manually specified lexical constraints, and a mutator iteratively rewrites top-performing candidates. Candidates are evaluated on disjoint training subsets, selected by top-K performance, and refined over multiple rounds. No gradients, logits, hidden states, or parameter updates are used; the procedure is fully black-box.

The important design choice is not search sophistication but the strict semantic exclusion. By aggressively removing task-related content from the prompt space, the paper tries to isolate non-semantic control factors such as tone, persona, ritual, protocol, or formatting. The paper then extends the analysis beyond accuracy gains to behavioral steering, showing that such prompts can bias the model toward first-option selection, wrong answers, or even/prime-number outputs in math settings. That makes the phenomenon more than a curiosity about odd prompts.5f:T4e8,The experiments cover reasoning and QA benchmarks, models from 0.8B to 27B, and three model families. The main result is that spurious prompts can match or outperform standard prompting baselines and PromptWizard, despite being intentionally stripped of task-specific semantics. The paper also argues that these prompts are semantically indistinguishable from unrelated text and are often shorter than task-aware optimized prompts, which weakens two simple explanations: that they are secretly task descriptions, or that they work merely because they are longer.

Transfer experiments are especially informative. The paper reports that effective spurious prompts often do not transfer cleanly across models or benchmarks, suggesting that they exploit highly specific interactions between a given model, a benchmark, and the prompt’s latent control structure. If they were simply activating a general reasoning mode, stronger transfer would be expected. The steering experiments are another key result because they show directional control, not just accidental performance variation.

The provided text does not include all absolute numbers, search hyperparameters, or benchmark-by-benchmark tables, but the setup appears systematic rather than anecdotal.60:T424,Start with the introduction to see how the paper distinguishes spurious prompts from ordinary prompt variation. Then read the search section carefully: the forbidden-vocabulary design, lexical filters, train/validation/test split, and the mechanism used to avoid overfitting prompt search to a small slice of data. If those controls are weak, the notion of spuriousness becomes much less convincing.

In the experiments, focus on three parts. First, comparisons against standard prompting and PromptWizard to judge whether the effect is broad or narrow. Second, the semantic-indistinguishability and length-control analyses, which test whether the prompts are truly unrelated on the surface. Third, the transfer and steering results, which say the most about mechanism. It is also worth checking whether the paper controls for benchmark formatting artifacts, answer-position priors, and decoding settings. A quick read of the method and main figures should take around 20 minutes; a deeper read should include prompt examples and failure cases in the appendix.61:T545,The evaluation uses three corpora: 700 MT-Consistency multiple-choice questions, 700 MMLU-Pro questions across 14 domains, and 700 GSM8K numeric problems. The model set includes Qwen3-32B with a think/no_think toggle, GPT-OSS-20B with an explicit reasoning channel, and Gemma-4-31B-it run without native thinking and with inline prompted CoT. For Qwen3-32B, the latent-correct rate at the first behavioral flip is close to 50% on the multiple-choice settings: 50.7% on MT-Consistency, 50.0% on MMLU-Pro, and 55.1% when the same questions are reformatted as short answers. GSM8K is lower at 32%, which the authors attribute to the tighter coupling between numeric reasoning and the final answer. Switching Qwen3-32B to no_think collapses the rate to 11-15%. GPT-OSS-20B shows a similar effect on MMLU-Pro at 52.9%, while Gemma-4-31B-it sits near the no_think baseline at 19-22%. An independent GPT-4o audit of 260 UC cells agrees with the in-house judge on 86%, abstains on 13%, and hard-disagrees on 1%. On 12,600 Qwen3-32B cells, the next-token argmax immediately before the emitted answer letter is the correct option in 84% of UC cases, with mean P(correct)=0.82. A naive repair that regenerates the answer from the trace conclusion reduces accuracy on the MCQ corpora, because pressured traces can also contain the attacker’s suggested option.62:T417,Starting from the LAR metric introduced in parameterization theory, the authors rewrite it as a log-overlap between two distributions. For a matrix W, the normalized squared singular values define a weight spectrum p. For a batch of inputs, the normalized squared projections onto the right singular directions of W define an activation spectrum q. High LAR means that both weights and activations concentrate on the same small set of directions. Low LAR means that one or both spectra are diffuse, or that the two are poorly aligned. The paper also provides covariance and correlation forms. Empirically, p and q remain highly correlated during training, so LAR often behaves as a measure of spectral spread. A useful derivation states that if the computation concentrates on k aligned singular directions, then LAR = 1 - 1/2 log_n k, giving k ≈ n^{2(1-LAR)} as an effective dimension estimate. The large-model analysis focuses on the unembedding matrix, which links hidden states to vocabulary logits and is sensitive to memorization behavior.63:T673,The experimental design is simple and well controlled. The authors select seven open-source reasoning-tuned models and assign fixed provider and receiver roles, with the main focus on stronger-to-weaker transfer. A provider first generates a full reasoning trace for a problem. Instead of evaluating only the full trace, the trace is then exposed to the receiver through cumulative prefixes of increasing length. For each prefix, the receiver is tested in two modes. In force-answer mode, it must answer directly from the available prefix, which isolates what can be extracted from the provided text alone. In free-generation mode, it may continue reasoning before answering, which tests whether the prefix can scaffold the receiver’s own reasoning process. The protocol is run on three benchmarks chosen for complementary transfer dynamics: AIME for derivation-heavy math with single integer answers, MMLU-Pro for knowledge-intensive multiple-choice reasoning, and ZebraLogic for constraint reasoning with structured multi-field outputs. This benchmark choice is central to the paper’s logic: AIME makes answer appearance easy to track, MMLU-Pro highlights receiver-intrinsic competence, and ZebraLogic reveals whether partial structured information accumulates before the full answer is available. The paper also studies an inference-time policy based on receiver agreement: if multiple receivers converge to the same answer from a partial prefix, the system can stop early instead of consuming the full provider trace. The authors further test whether agreement that persists across consecutive prefixes is more reliable than one-off agreement.64:T628,The main findings come in three layers. First, full traces often do transfer successfully across models, but that fact alone is not diagnostic of mechanism. Second, prefix trajectories reveal benchmark-specific patterns. On AIME, force-answer and free-generation diverge sharply: in force-answer mode, receivers usually become correct only after the final answer is already present in the prefix, while in free-generation mode they often succeed earlier by continuing from partial reasoning. This is the paper’s clearest result, because it shows that successful full-trace transfer does not necessarily mean the receiver has benefited from the provider’s reasoning process; sometimes it simply reads off the answer. On MMLU-Pro, transfer depends more strongly on the receiver’s own competence and prior knowledge, so shorter prefixes can already be sufficient. On ZebraLogic, the useful signal often comes from progressively accumulated partial structured answers rather than explicit final-answer leakage alone. Third, the agreement-based stopping experiments show that early stopping can retain much of the transfer benefit, and that agreement is substantially more reliable when the same answer remains stable across consecutive prefix lengths. The excerpt provided here does not include the full result tables, so exact accuracies, prefix thresholds, and token savings cannot be reproduced faithfully in this summary. The value of the experiments lies less in headline numbers and more in the shape of the transfer curves and what those curves imply about mechanism.65:T8fd,方法上最关键的设计有三层。第一层是任务构造。作者选了 graph coloring 和 Sudoku 两个程序化生成、可渲染成图像的任务。它们既需要从图像中读取结构化信息，也需要在此基础上做离散推理，适合把感知和推理拆开。每个样本都配有一个 canonical textual perception 表示 p*，完整保留完成任务所需的视觉信息。模型输出被强制写成“先 perception，后 reasoning”的格式，因此可以直接比较模型生成的 perception 与 oracle perception 是否完全一致，并进一步做 counterfactual reasoning evaluation：把真实 perception 喂给模型，看它在“看对了”的前提下能否推理对。

第二层是机制分析。对 SFT，作者不是只看 token 数，而是同时统计 perception token 占比、loss 占比和梯度范数占比。以 Qwen3-VL 在 graph coloring 上为例，perception 只占 2.5% 的 CoT token，却只贡献 1.3% 的 loss、8.5% 的 gradient norm，说明训练信号确实被 reasoning 主导。随后他们做 loss reweighting，把 perception 部分乘以不同权重，验证感知准确率会随权重上升而改善，但 reasoning 会下降，形成平滑 trade-off。为了避免手工调参，他们进一步引入动态多任务平衡方法，自动调 perception/reasoning 的权重。

对 RL，作者分析的是 reward coupling。标准 outcome reward 只看最终答对与否，因此它与 reasoning correctness 的相关性高，与 perception correctness 的相关性低。文中报告多数设置下，reward 与 reasoning correctness 的相关系数在 0.65 到 1.00 之间，而与 perception correctness 只有 0.34 到 0.43。于是他们加入显式 perception reward，或者用已有工作中的 surrogate reward 近似感知奖励，再观察端到端、感知、推理三者如何变化。结果同样出现 trade-off：感知奖励加大后，perception 提升，但 reasoning 可能受损。

第三层是干预验证。SFT 侧，作者比较固定重加权和动态平衡；RL 侧，比较真实 perception reward 与 surrogate reward。这里的重点不是某个具体权重最好，而是证明“训练信号分配”就是造成不对称优化的主要原因，而不是模型架构本身天然更擅长推理。66:T94c,The method has three important layers. First is task construction. The authors use graph coloring and Sudoku rendered as images. Both require reading structured visual information and then performing discrete reasoning on top of it. Each sample comes with a canonical textual perception representation p*, which fully captures the visual information needed for the task. Model outputs are constrained into a perception-first, reasoning-second format, so perception can be directly scored by exact match against the oracle representation. This also enables counterfactual reasoning evaluation: feed the model the ground-truth perception and measure whether it can reason correctly once perception is no longer the bottleneck.

Second is mechanism analysis. For SFT, the paper goes beyond token counts and measures token share, loss share, and gradient-norm share of the perception segment. On Qwen3-VL for graph coloring, perception occupies only 2.5% of CoT tokens, contributes 1.3% of the loss, and 8.5% of the gradient norm. This shows that optimization is heavily dominated by reasoning tokens. The authors then apply loss reweighting to the perception segment. Perception improves as its weight increases, but reasoning degrades, yielding a smooth trade-off. To avoid manual tuning, they also test dynamic multi-task balancing methods that adaptively adjust perception vs reasoning weights.

For RL, the key concept is reward coupling. Standard outcome rewards only depend on final correctness, so they correlate strongly with reasoning correctness but much less with perception correctness. Reported correlations are r=0.65-1.00 for reasoning and only r=0.34-0.43 for perception in most settings. The authors then add explicit perception rewards, and also test surrogate rewards from prior work when ground-truth perception rewards are unavailable. Again, the intervention exposes a trade-off: stronger perception reward improves perception but can weaken reasoning.

Third is intervention-based validation. On the SFT side, they compare fixed reweighting and dynamic balancing. On the RL side, they compare oracle perception rewards and surrogate rewards. The point is not that one specific weighting scheme wins everywhere, but that training-signal allocation itself explains the asymmetry much better than a vague claim that the architecture is simply better at reasoning.67:T788,Experiments cover two open VLM families, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5, on graph coloring and Sudoku. The most informative results come in several groups.

First, the baseline diagnosis. Under both SFT and RL, reasoning accuracy improves much more than perception accuracy. Moreover, when conditioned on oracle perception, reasoning is often already fairly strong, which means end-to-end failures are still dominated by perception. This pattern is stable across both model families and both tasks.

Second, evidence for token imbalance in SFT. On Qwen3-VL for graph coloring, perception tokens account for only 2.5% of the sequence, but only 1.3% of the loss and 8.5% of the gradient norm. Increasing the perception loss weight raises perception accuracy and lowers reasoning accuracy, but end-to-end accuracy peaks at a modest nonzero upweighting. Relative to standard SFT, this gives up to +13.8 points. Dynamic multi-task balancing improves further, reaching up to +18.2 points over standard SFT.

Third, evidence for reward coupling in RL. Standard outcome reward correlates with reasoning correctness at r=0.65-1.00, but with perception correctness at only r=0.34-0.43. Adding perception reward shifts optimization toward perception; in most settings, end-to-end performance peaks at a nonzero perception-reward weight, with gains up to +6.0 points over standard RL. When oracle perception reward is unavailable, surrogate rewards can still help. The paper evaluates several existing surrogate designs and finds that reward-perception correlation is a useful predictor of whether a surrogate will improve perception. The strongest surrogate gives +3.2 points.

The experimental style is controlled rather than broad. The paper is not trying to win on many benchmarks. It is trying to establish a causal chain: diagnose asymmetry, propose a mechanism, intervene on that mechanism, and observe the resulting trade-off and optimum.68:T465,For a quick read, start with the introduction and the task formulation. The whole paper depends on understanding how perception and reasoning are disentangled in both outputs and evaluation. Then focus on three sets of figures and tables:
1. The comparison among end-to-end accuracy, perception accuracy, and reasoning accuracy under oracle perception. This tells you where the actual bottleneck sits.
2. The SFT token/loss/gradient allocation analysis and the perception-weight sweep. This is where the optimization argument becomes concrete rather than intuitive.
3. The RL reward-correlation analysis and the perception-reward sweep. The most reusable idea here is the correlation-based diagnostic, not a particular reward formula.

Expected reading time is about 30-45 minutes. If the goal is only to extract the main lesson, read the introduction, analysis framework, SFT mechanism section, RL mechanism section, and conclusion. If the goal is to adapt the idea to your own training setup, pay closer attention to the output-format design, the counterfactual evaluation protocol, and how dynamic balancing is integrated.69:T49d,The authors first run three routing probes. They compare native refusal continuations with teacher-forced compliant continuations for the same harmful prompts. They test whether refusal-enforced requests change the routing of benign prompts. They also create benign counterparts that preserve topic and surface form while removing unsafe intent, which separates topical specialization from harmful intent. In all three settings, routing changes induced by safety behavior or intent are smaller than changes induced by topic. Motivated by this, they introduce RASET, Router-Agnostic Safety-critical Expert Tuning. RASET identifies candidate experts using a contrastive routing-sensitivity score: activation on harmful instructions minus activation on benign instructions. This suppresses topic-general experts and highlights experts more specifically associated with harmful-request processing. It then applies parameter-efficient tuning only to the selected experts, while freezing the router, shared components, and all non-selected experts. The design directly tests whether localized expert representations can alter safety behavior without changing the model’s routing logic.6a:T48a,The diagnostic is tested on Llama-family 8B, 70B, and 405B checkpoints with controlled relations of arity r=3 to r=6. True relation tuples show stronger orientation-sign consistency at the expected rank k=r than scrambled tuples. The 405B model gives the most uniform pattern: multi-template audits keep positive diagonal margins for both argument-only and predicate-plus-argument constructors. Smaller checkpoints show positive support but with more dependence on templates and constructors. The steering assay uses clean and corrupt edge-grid prompts that share row and column scaffolds and answer format but differ in YES/NO relation markers. In 70B and 405B, moving the corrupt relation-marker cloud toward the clean one at patch layer 5 recovers both clean-answer behavior and residual relation geometry at readout layer 35. Shape-only, centroid-plus-shape, and Grassmann-shape paths work well, while centroid-only and equal-norm controls do not. Site and ordering audits indicate that the effect is not just patching important marker positions: clean shapes transfer, whereas corrupt-donor shapes, broken frames, and wrong-site placebos remain much weaker.6b:T55c,A three-stage pipeline that separates “verifiability” from “causal executability”.
1) Answer-aware Tutor, backward chaining: given the ground-truth answer, the Tutor constructs a backward chain of shell commands whose executions retrieve supporting evidence step by step. Backward construction makes multi-hop questions easier because each hop can be anchored to executable string/entity matches and hard-verified by command outputs.
2) Answer-blind Planner, forward causalization: at inference time the agent cannot see the answer; it must act based only on observable history (previous commands and returned snippets). The Planner generates forward reasoning traces and commands from the observable state, and the Tutor aligns them to the verified backward chain, producing trajectories that are both causally grounded and guided toward a known-good search path.
3) GRPO refinement: starting from the cold-start policy, the agent is further improved via Group Relative Policy Optimization through direct interaction with the corpus. The paper’s motivation is that naïve RL tends to collapse into degenerate behaviors, so strong initialization is required before online optimization.

The key lesson is that parallel multi-token prediction needs structured candidate exploration and hardware-aware budgeting; otherwise, the gain from parallelism is partly lost through low acceptance.","technical_approach":"Bastion introduces tree-structured block-diffusion drafting. The diffusion drafter produces candidate distributions for a future block in one parallel step. The system has three main components. An acceptance surrogate estimates expected accepted length from path confidence scores under the drafter distributions. An online latency estimator predicts verification cost using a hardware-aware roofline model calibrated with observed runtimes. A best-first expansion procedure grows the tree only while the expected acceptance gain justifies the extra verification cost. Compared with static tree methods, the topology is query-dependent and budget-aware. 损失了多少本可获得的投票收益”。\n\n数据选择也比较讲究。作者没有用单一 gold label 的普通 benchmark，而是用 ChaosNLI 系列，因为每个样本有 100 个人工标注，可以得到更稳的人类多数标签，同时还能利用人类熵分析样本难度和歧义。主实验覆盖 MNLI、SNLI、AlphaNLI，并额外在 RewardBench 的 pairwise preference 任务上做验证。judge panel 由 9 个前沿 LLM 组成，来自 7 个模型家族。作者还系统检查 prompt variant、temperature 等设置，避免结论只是某个 prompt 的偶然现象。最后，他们测试了常见聚合方法，如 Dawid-Skene EM 和 accuracy-weighted voting，检验“更聪明的 aggregation”能否弥补相关性问题。","experiments":"主结果很直接。9 个 judge 的 panel，在三套 NLI 数据上只提供大约 2.0–2.5 个独立投票的信息量。也就是说，名义上 9 票，统计上接近 2 票。对应地，真实 panel 准确率比独立投票假设下的 Condorcet 预测低 8–22 个百分点，而且 permutation test 给出 p < 1e-4。更关键的是，panel 几乎不能稳定超过单个最佳 judge：在 MNLI 上，panel 72.0%，最好单模型 Qwen3-32B 为 71.8%，只高 0.2pp，基本在噪声内；在 SNLI 上，最好单模型 Claude Sonnet 4.5 为 84.2%，panel 只有 77.7%；在 AlphaNLI 上，最好单模型 91.2%，panel 88.7%。\n\n稳健性方面，这个独立性缺口在不同任务、prompt 版本、temperature 设置下都很稳定；RewardBench 上 n_eff 也只有 2.0。扩展曲线显示，judge 数量超过 5 之后边际收益很小，有效独立性大致在 2.3–3.1 左右饱和。聚合算法方面，即便给到 oracle gold labels，Dawid-Skene 和 accuracy-weighted voting 也只能弥补最多约 11% 的 Condorcet gap，说明瓶颈不是投票规则太简单，而是输入错误本身高度共线。这个负结果很有分量，因为它否定了“换个 aggregation 就能救 panel”的常见直觉。","reading_guide":"泛读建议 20 分钟左右。先看 Introduction 和主结果表，抓住两个数字：n_eff 约 2，以及 Condorcet gap 8–22pp。然后看方法部分里 error correlation、Kish effective sample size 和 Condorcet null model 的定义，理解作者如何把“相关错误”变成可量化对象。接着看 replication 和 robustness：MNLI、SNLI、AlphaNLI、RewardBench，以及 prompt/temperature 变化是否保持同样结论。最后看 aggregation baseline 那一节，因为它回答了一个最自然的反问：是不是多数投票太粗糙。若只想快速判断是否值得引用，重点看三处：panel vs best single judge 的对比表、n_eff 结果、aggregation 无法补救的实验。","authors_note":""},"summary_en":{"core_problem":"The paper asks a basic but underexamined question about LLM-as-a-judge panels: when multiple frontier models vote on an evaluation item, how PRM/过程奖励模型、检测器、似然统计、hidden-state 统计或手工启发式，但必须在独立数据上训练/固定，避免把校准集信息泄漏进 proxy。\n- 标注：每步有二值错误标注 Yt，定义首个错误位置 F(Z)=min{t:Yt=1}。\n- 目标：给定风险水平 α，用 split conformal 的交换性假设（实例级 等论证角色，以及 Flavell 元认知框架中的 monitoring 一类成分。模型骨干选 DeBERTa-v3-base，不用更长上下文的 ModernBERT，理由是这里输入是句级短文本，细粒度分类精度更重要。分类头是 8 维 sigmoid 多标签输出，用 BCEWithLogitsLoss 训练，并对类别不平衡做了软化权重。训练集约 10 万句 reasoning Labels come from reviewer soundness sub-scores rather than acceptance decisions or overall ratings. The curation pipeline uses reviewer-agreement filtering, near-verbatim proposal extraction from source papers, retrieval-backed atomic-claim auditing, and outcome masking so that models are evaluated on information plausibly available before execution. addresses a precise but often blurred issue in correctness-based RL with verifiable rewards: what objective is actually being optimized, and how the stochastic update induced by a finite rollout group relates to that objective. Prior work such as MaxRL connects RLVR to maximum likelihood, but mostly through asymptotics or first-order approximations. RL2ML focuses on the practical regime where each prompt gets only a finite number of rollouts and training runs for a finite horizon. In that regime, 'more ML-like' is not automatically optimal. extractor（QuCo-extractor-0.5B）从句子中抽取 (head, relation, tail)，只保留第一个有效 triplet，并丢弃 relation，只用 head/tail。第二，把两个实体规约成 content words，减少表面形式差异带来的漏检。第三，把这些词作为 AND 查询送到基于 Infini-gram 的 Wikipedia 索引，在 advantage 结合起来训练策略。这样既保留最终答案目标，又给中间关键行为更细的奖励。和 ARPO 这类基于树采样的 step-level 方法相比，SAPO 不需要为每个中间节点展开大量 continuation，因此训练效率更高。\n\n这个方法的关键假设也很明确：训练时能拿到答案，并能构造质量尚可的 ER The next stage then uses ordinary cross-entropy SFT on the new task data plus this buffer. No teacher forward pass, auxiliary KL loss, or current-task target rewriting is required. OPR-RU uses task-specific evaluation rules as the reward. OPR-SC removes the need for labels by ranking generations using the model’s own length-normalized log probability. The mechanism is that replay samples are drawn from the previous model and filtered for quality, so the replay gradient pulls the updated model toward the previous policy on historical prompts. This differs from SDFT, OPSD, and GKD, which inject the signal through objective-side distillation, and from RazorSFT, which rewrites current-task targets rather than maintaining an on-policy cross-task buffer.","experiments":"The experiments use three 7B–8B instruction-tuned backbones: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B, and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct. It replaces this with a probability-based scoring rule that uses smoother criterion-level satisfaction probabilities. This is useful for reasoning cold-start recipes, small high-quality SFT datasets, and cases where an SFT checkpoint explores less effectively than the base model. The contribution is not a pretraining method, but it gives a concrete token-level view of how post-training can preserve or damage capabilities acquired during pretraining.","technical_approach":"The proposed method, Entropy-KL Selective Fine-Tuning, modifies the SFT objective by masking tokens that are likely to be harmful supervision. Tokens with high predictive entropy are treated as uncertain and therefore risky to imitate directly in a low-data regime. Tokens with high KL divergence from a reference model are treated as likely to induce excessive policy drift. The remaining tokens are used for the standard likelihood loss. EKSFT also adds entropy regularization to reduce entropy collapse and KL regularization to keep the policy close to the reference distribution. Compared with methods such as PSFT, IW-SFT, ASFT, or mixed SFT/RL objectives, the main distinction is that EKSFT decides at token level which parts of the expert response should contribute to supervised learning, instead of supervising all tokens with only a global constraint.","experiments":"The experimental setup follows an SFT-then-RL pipeline. EKSFT is then compared against standard SFT and several baselines designed to control policy drift or combine SFT and RL signals. The reported pattern is that EKSFT gives a better initialization and improves the subsequent RL stage across multiple benchmarks. The provided material does not include full numerical tables, so exact gains should be verified from the results section. At inference time, the model is expected to infer the latent reward structure from the context, rather than updating parameters or selecting from a fixed bank of reward models. The key technical claim is negative first: with only binary pairwise labels, unseen reward parameters are not identifiable in general. Different latent rewards can induce the same observed choices. The paper then adds human response time, motivated by cognitive decision models where easier decisions tend to be faster and near-ties tend to be slower. Response time gives a proxy for reward margin, complementing the direction supplied by the binary label. This changes the adaptation problem from under-specified comparison learning to a better-constrained latent reward inference problem.","experiments":"The experiments cover synthetic preference settings and real human decision-making data. First, the authors reproduce the behavioral retention gap using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. The model is adapted to scientific QA with completion-only SFT, then further optimized with Dr.GRPO. The RL setup uses group size 64, two refinement steps, and no explicit KL penalty. Second, they identify circuits with Differential Binary Masking. DBM learns sparse head-level masks that interpolate between base and counterfactual activations, optimizing the probability of a target answer while penalizing mask size. Third, they compare masks discovered in the base, SFT, and RL models. A head is treated as differentially vulnerable when its mask weight is substantially lower after SFT than after RL. RL stays closer to the base model and preserves more retention performance, while sometimes under-optimizing the new task. The mask is designed to identify which modified weight entries are necessary for maintaining an edit. It is optimized with three constraints: restore the original fact by making the pruned edited model prefer the old object over the new one; remove as few weights as possible; and preserve the model’s general behavior. The key test is to train one mask across semantically diverse edits. If edits were fact-specific at the level of critical parameters, such a mask should not generalize. If the same mask reverses unseen edits, then different edits rely on a common functional structure. The follow-up analysis suggests that the mask removes amplified attention signals in later layers, while MLP pathways carrying the original fact remain intact.","experiments":"A single small mask, typically pruning less than 10% of the edited weights, reverses more than 80% of edits on the training set and more than 70% on held-out edits. This supports the claim that diverse edits share critical weight positions. A stronger necessity test applies the mask before the editing procedure; edit success drops from about 98% to 38%, indicating that the same mechanism is not only sufficient for reversal but also important for producing successful edits. The mechanistic analysis points to reduced over-attention to the injected edited signal in later layers, rather than removal of factual content from the MLP pathway.","reading_guide":"Skim in about 20–30 minutes.
